First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $2-\text{i}$ to get rid of the fraction and isolate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{6+13\text{i}}{5} & =\frac{p+\text{i}q}{2-\text{i}} \\ \frac{1}{5}(6+13\text{i})(2-\text{i}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{1}{5}(12-6\text{i}+26\text{i}-13{\text{i}}^{2}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{1}{5}(12+13+20\text{i}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{1}{5}(25+20\text{i}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ 5+4\text{i} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get

$$
5=p.
$$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =q.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=5$ and $q=4.$
